title: Honcho ingest record (v0)
description: One source record for Honcho's ingest API: a line of a JSONL file for `honcho ingest import`, or an item of the `records` array of `POST /v3/workspaces/{workspace_id}/ingest`: a record to ingest (`op` left out, or `upsert`), or a record the source deleted (`op: delete`). Experimental: v0 may still change. Unknown fields are rejected, as `honcho ingest import` and the SDKs reject them; the API itself ignores them.

IngestContainer.description: Where a record lives in its source: a channel, a thread, a repository.

id.description: The container's ID in the source
id.title: Id

parent_id.description: The parent container's ID, e.g. a thread's channel
parent_id.title: Parent Id

IngestContainer.title: IngestContainer

IngestParticipant.description: A person on a record. The `id` is what connects them across records.

id.description: The person's ID in the source, if it has one
id.title: Id

handle.description: The account's username in the source, unique there: a GitHub login, a Discord username. Used only to suggest which accounts are one person.
handle.title: Handle

aliases.description: Other names the account goes by, such as a profile name or a server nickname. Used only to suggest which accounts are one person.
aliases.title: Aliases

email.description: The account's email address. Ingest keeps only a digest of it, scoped to the workspace, to suggest which accounts are one person; the address itself is not stored. A value that isn't an address is ignored.
email.title: Email

bot.description: The source marks this account as a bot or an integration. Ingest creates its peer with `observe_me` off, so nothing is derived about it; its messages are still stored and read as context.
bot.title: Bot

IngestParticipant.title: IngestParticipant

IngestRecordCreate.description: One source record to ingest, or a newer version of one already ingested.

op.description: `upsert`, the default: ingest the record, or replace it with a newer version (a later `revised_at`) during the dry run
op.title: Op

source_instance.description: The server, team or account inside the source
source_instance.title: Source Instance

source_id.description: The record's ID in that instance. Without it, the record is identified by a hash of its content, so only identical content dedups; sources whose records can change must send it.
source_id.title: Source Id

revised_at.description: When the source last changed this record
revised_at.title: Revised At

container.description: Where the record lives; omit for a standalone record

author.description: Who wrote it; omit when there is no single author

session_id.description: An explicit session, used instead of mapping the container
session_id.title: Session Id

peer_id.description: An explicit author peer, used instead of mapping the author
peer_id.title: Peer Id

IngestRecordCreate.title: IngestRecordCreate

IngestRecordDelete.description:
A record the source deleted.

During the workspace's dry run its message is removed and a tombstone kept,
so the record never comes back; a delete for a record not seen yet leaves a
tombstone too. After the dry run it's refused. A delete is final: a later
version of the record is refused.

source_instance.description: The server, team or account inside the source
source_instance.title: Source Instance

source_id.description: The deleted record's ID in that instance
source_id.title: Source Id

revised_at.description: When the source deleted it. A delete older than the stored version changes nothing
revised_at.title: Revised At

IngestRecordDelete.title: IngestRecordDelete

MessageConfiguration.description:
The set of options that can be in a message DB-level configuration dictionary.

All fields are optional. Message-level configuration overrides all other configurations.
MessageConfiguration.title: MessageConfiguration

custom_instructions.description: Custom instructions for the deriver. Overrides the top-level custom_instructions at the same level. Set to an empty string to explicitly use none.
custom_instructions.title: Custom Instructions
